styleReference: User-approved moderate-detail landscape drafts: hail (17.jpg) and sleet (18.jpg).
prompt: Use image 1 ONLY as the scene/composition reference to restyle. Images 2 and 3 are the USER-APPROVED STYLE REFERENCES (hail and sleet). Create ONE 16:9 landscape weather illustration, target 1280x720, matching the exact MODERATE woodblock detail level of images 2 and 3. Broad printed color planes, subtle fine paper grain, atmospheric layered silhouettes, recognizable but selectively drawn architecture, irregular foliage clusters, restrained roof structure, calm quieter sky and ground, a limited number of broad broken reflections. Preserve the main motifs and wide composition of image 1 while reducing its fine clutter to the approved references' level. Do not over-simplify into geometric clip art or flat icon silhouettes: keep enough handcrafted architectural and vegetation character to match the approved examples. Do not add dense stippling, detailed individual leaves, rows of roof tiles, elaborate carved ornament, tiny masonry grids, excessive ripples, photographic shading or glossy digital gradients. Restrained warm ivory, pale blue-grey, slate blue, deep navy and small vermilion accents; translate vivid green and pink into the approved palette. Weather and cloud coverage must match the specified condition, not the storm weather of the style references. For non-rainy codes keep the ground appropriate and do not copy wet streets, snow, rain, hail or dark storm sky from style references. No text, labels, icons, border, panels, watermark or signature. Opaque full bleed landscape.
